title: task complete rejects --final-summary and blames the actor for it
description:
`quest task complete <id> --final-summary "..."` is rejected, so writing a final summary at completion time requires two commands (`task edit --final-summary` then `task complete`). Reported by opum-marketplace while closing OMARK-42.

Verified 2026-09-11 against quest 0.6.0 in a scratch workspace:

  quest task complete T-1 --final-summary "done" --actor jdn --actor-kind human --json
  -> exit 2, {"error_type":"usage","message":"task complete requires a reference and an explicit actor."}

  quest task complete T-1 --actor jdn --actor-kind human --json
  -> exit 6, validation (an unrelated illegal-transition error) -- so the actor and reference parse fine

The diagnostic is the sharper half of this bug and was not in the original report. Both a reference and an explicit actor WERE supplied; the unknown flag is what failed. The message names two things the caller got right and says nothing about the one they got wrong, which sends them to re-check their actor declaration -- the most heavily ritualised part of a Quest write -- instead of to the flag. `quest help task complete` does list the accepted flags (--actor, --actor-kind, --accountable-human) and its usage line omits --final-summary, so the information exists; it is the error path that does not use it.

Two candidate fixes, not mutually exclusive, and choosing between them is this task's job:

A. Accept --final-summary on `task complete`. quest instructions task-finalization treats writing a final summary and moving to a terminal status as one step, so the two-command shape is a seam the workflow does not have. task complete already mutates the record; folding the summary in is not a new capability, and a single write also removes a window where a task is Done with no summary.

B. Make the usage error name the actual cause -- report the unrecognised flag, not a generic reference-and-actor sentence. This is worth doing even if A lands, because the same generic message will misdirect the next caller who mistypes any other flag. Check whether other commands share this message and misreport the same way; if so the fix belongs at the shared parser, not here.

Recommend both: A removes the two-command shape, B stops the parser lying about why a command failed.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A final summary can be written and the task moved to a terminal status without the caller needing two separate writes, OR the usage line and help output state plainly that --final-summary is not accepted on task complete and name the command that does accept it.
A quest task complete invocation carrying an unrecognised flag reports the unrecognised flag, and does not report a missing reference or actor when both were supplied.
Whether the misleading usage message is shared with other commands is established and stated; if it is shared, the fix lands at the shared parser rather than being patched per command.
A test covers the unrecognised-flag path asserting on the diagnostic content, not only on exit code 2 -- exit 2 was already correct here and is what made the wrong message survive.

implementationNotes: Second sighting of the same shared usage-error path (reported by opum-agent, 2026-09-12): `quest task edit <id> --implementation-notes "..."` also fails with no flag named -- `{"error_type":"usage","message":"task edit received invalid arguments."}`, exit 2. `--implementation-notes` is a real flag on `task create` but task edit has no such flag; its append-equivalent is `--add-note` (confirmed via `quest help task create` vs `quest help task edit`). This is the same shared usage-error path as the task-complete case already in this task's description, not command-specific: it strengthens AC #2/#3 (the message should name the unrecognised flag, and the fix likely belongs at the shared parser). The create/edit flag-name asymmetry is what makes the missing flag name expensive here: a caller who knows --implementation-notes from task create has no way to learn from the error that task edit spells it --add-note.

Direct literal reproduction (opum-agent, 2026-09-12), the exact case this task was filed for, not an analog:

  quest task complete OPAG-109 --final-summary "..." --actor opum-agent-orchestrator --actor-kind delegated-agent --accountable-human jdnewhouse
  -> {"error_type":"usage","message":"task complete requires a reference and an explicit actor.","principal":null}, exit 2

Reference and all three actor flags were present and correct; --final-summary is simply not a flag task complete accepts. Cost in practice: the caller read the message as an actor-declaration problem, checked their flags, found them correct, and only found the real cause by rerunning bare (the first run was piped, so the JSON error vanished and the write looked like a silent no-op). Worked around with task edit --final-summary then task complete (both exit 0, record ends Done with summary attached) -- useful as the fix's test shape.

Third confirmed sighting of the same shared usage-error path, after task edit --implementation-notes (see prior note). Reinforces AC #2/#3 further: task complete --final-summary, task edit --implementation-notes, and whatever else shares this path all misreport the same way.
